item.title: New Microsoft Defender 'ShieldCrash' zero-day grants SYSTEM access
item.description: A local privilege-escalation bug in Windows Defender lets any process reach SYSTEM, and it's already being exploited before a patch exists.

item.title: ClearFake WebDAV infection chain delivers Amatera stealer, ZigCryptoStealer, and NetSupport Manager
item.description: Problem: Attackers need to plant stealer malware while dodging disk-based antivirus and EDR. Approach: A fake CAPTCHA tricks the victim into running a command that loads a disguised DLL over WebDAV via rundll32, so nothing touches disk. One branch uses a blockchain contract as an unblockable dead-drop for its command server; the other uses a fixed server in Russia. Both abuse a vulnerable signed driver to kill security tools. Result: Talos mapped two chains delivering crypto-theft malware (Amatera, ZigCryptoStealer) or a remote-access tool (NetSupport Manager). Why it matters: disk-based AV misses memory-only execution; watch for WebDAV-triggered rundll32 and odd driver loads. Glossary: WebDAV, BYOVD (abusing a vulnerable driver for kernel access), dead-drop resolver, ClickFix (fake-verification social engineering).

item.title: F5 BIG-IP APM Malware Injects a PHP Web Shell Into Memory, Evading Disk Scans
item.description: Attackers are hiding a memory-resident PHP web shell inside BIG-IP APM devices specifically to dodge disk-based malware scans.

item.title: Almost 1,900 Blizzard workers vote through a "historic" union contract securing protections against layoffs and gen-AI
item.description: Blizzard's newly unionized workers won contract language giving them a voice on AI adoption and stronger layoff protections, a rare foothold for labor over generative-AI decisions in games.

item.title: No Man's Sky's 10th anniversary update will let you rule space stations, built floating orbital bases and go on holiday to the sun
item.description: Ten years on, No Man's Sky adds ownable space stations and orbital base-building, showing how far a disastrous launch can be walked back with sustained updates.

item.title: AI Has Solved One of Math's $1 Million Millennium Prize Problems
item.description: An AI system reportedly cracked one of math's seven Millennium Prize Problems, worth $1 million, a genuine result rather than a benchmark claim, if it holds up to verification.

item.title: Beryllium signal identifies stars that have swallowed rocky planets
item.description: Elevated beryllium in certain stars gives astronomers a chemical fingerprint for identifying ones that swallowed a rocky planet.

item.title: Reverse Engineering The Philips PM5139
item.description: A hobbyist reverse-engineered a Philips PM5139 test instrument, documenting the teardown and reconstructed internals for others who own the hardware.

item.title: Decoding the NEC V20 Microcode ROM
item.description: Problem: A cycle-accurate emulator of the 1980s NEC V20 chip needs its real microcode, which exists only as ~30,000 bits baked into the physical die. Approach: A hobbyist photographed the die and tried an existing bit-extraction tool, but low image contrast made it unreliable, so they trained a small neural network on about 1,000 hand-labeled bit images to classify each cell as 0 or 1, then manually checked the unclear ones. Result: A largely-automated, published decode of the ROM, letting the V20's exact internal behavior be matched instruction by instruction. Why it matters: Turns emulation from guesswork into a verified match to real silicon, and revisits the old NEC/Intel compatibility dispute. Glossary: Microcode ROM, die shot, cycle-accurate emulation, CNN.

item.title: Factoring RSA 260
item.description: A writeup on factoring the 260-digit RSA challenge number, a marker of how far practical integer-factoring capability has advanced.
